The court must also find prejudice under *Strickland v. Washington*: a reasonable probability that, without the counsel error and with the improperly admitted evidence excluded, the outcome would have been different. That means reweighing the excluded evidence against the rest of the trial record and asking whether the remaining evidence still undermines confidence in the verdict (*Kimmelman v. Morrison*, 477 U.S. 365 (1986)). A finding that the objection would have succeeded satisfies the merit component, but it does not establish prejudice by itself.

CONFIDENCE: 90
